sections.title: Container build steps
sections.what: Describes the three stages: installing packages, building the web page, and assembling the small final image that serves it on port 3000.
sections.why: Likely reason: separate stages keep the build tools out of the final image.
sections.watch_out: Only package.json is copied in the first stage, so a lock file would need to be added here for repeatable installs.

summary: A build recipe that packages the Next.js web page into a container that serves it on port 3000.
purpose: Lets the owner run the web frontend in a container on any machine that has Docker.
why: Likely reason: a container gives the same setup everywhere, and the stages keep the final image small.
how: The first stage installs packages from the package file. The second stage copies the source and builds the site. The third stage creates the final image with only the built output, runs as a non-administrator user, and starts the Node server on port 3000.
inputs: The package.json file and the rest of the frontend source, including any settings files in the folder.
outputs: A container image that serves the frontend on port 3000.
risks: Only package.json is copied before installing, and no lock file is copied, so package versions may differ between builds. The server address is fixed at build time to its default value. Copying the whole folder may bring secret settings into the build stage. The final step needs a standalone output setting in the Next.js config, which this file does not show.
debug: If the build fails, read the logs of the install and build stages. If the page cannot reach the server, check the address set at build time. If the container starts with no page, check the standalone output exists.
